constraints: Attach to the sole owner-managed local environment. Never launch another application or change NyxID configuration.
Two real EG processes and two Ready coordinated AMs sharing isolated storage; exact source and image bindings must accompany evidence.
Synthetic local platform and provider only. A local relay result is not a production bot or real third-party-platform acceptance result.
Acquire creates bounded fixture configuration only, never executes the feature under test. Public cleanup must be registered before mutation; reconcile unknown outcomes using the original key.
Adapters return observed raw fields and receipts, never PASS booleans or a runCase implementation. Missing methods throw BLOCKED.
Credentials stay in the adapter; request and observation records must omit secrets, sealed capabilities and raw identities. No Secret reads, pod exec, production writes or customer bots.

Real EG HTTP with safe credential injection inside adapter; expected status codes are forwarded. eg_receipt is a distinct EG receipt with actual c275-eg-serving-v1 snapshots before/after, request_id, method, status, started_at, ended_at and attribution; never AM ownership.
eg.configuration: Read actual saved producer configuration -> {platform,trustMode,issuer,keyId,routeId,callbackPath,verificationMode,durableCustomExecution,partition}; no credentials.
eg.platformSend: Send the specified synthetic platform wire event through the real verified ingress; return {platform,trustMode,eventId,conversationId,responseId,agentId,consumerId,egInstance,destination,expectedSender,expectedContentDigest,status|outcome}. Negative variants return explicit rejected/refused/ignored and no turn; expected fields derive from independently seeded inputs.
eg.waitForTurn: Observe bounded real provider/AM acceptance and return {eventId,conversationId,responseId,agentId,consumerId,servingAm,owningAm,epoch,providerAccepted,turnCount,effectCount,amRequests}. Both-AM attribution must be independently observed and each Agent-bound event routed through non-owner ingress. Required amRequests:[{am,request_id,status,elapsed_ms,serving,serving_after,started_at,ended_at,attribution,agent_id_sha256,owner_proof}] from actual parent NonOwnerRouter; proof includes request_id, ingress, owner, owner_epoch, kind, verdict and instance hashes. No reconstructed requested labels. egReceipts remain separately attributed to EG processes.
eg.waitForDelivery: Read synthetic platform's actual delivery capture -> {eventId,responseId,destination,sender,contentDigest,status,count,contextEventIds}. Do not infer delivery from 202 or provider acceptance.
eg.replayEvent: Resubmit identical retained signed bytes/key through requested EG replica, preserving event identity.
eg.recoverResponse: Read/reconnect the retained response via peer AM without new admission -> same turn fields plus recoveryMode:read_existing,resubmissions:0.
eg.counters: Independent provider/platform counts of actual turns/effects, scoped to this fixture.
eg.quiesce: Bounded no-late-effect barrier after rejected input; return actual counters. A sleep alone is insufficient.
eg.drain: Bounded finality with actual {turns,deliveries,pending,unknown,lateEffects}; never treat timeout as success.
eg.events: Seeded disposable event(s) include the original eventRef, eventId, bindingId, bindingGeneration, consumerId, conversationId, destination, expiry and independent expected activity/artifact digest. Never return credentials. event_context itself submits the tested event.
eg.captureEffects: captureEffects({key?,eventId?,kind?}) returns actual synthetic platform effects with destination/contentDigest. No predicted effects.
eg.dropReplyResponse: Submit one reply with the given frozen key/body then drop only the response after actual acceptance; return outcome:unknown. This is one real POST, never an adapter retry.
eg.reconcileReply: Read retained activity/receipt for the original key through the peer; return {key,delivery,sendAttempts}. Never resend.
eg.continuationReceipts: Read independent AM/provider/platform receipts for the specified event -> [{attachmentIndex,kind,responseId,status,delivery}].
eg.keyMetadata: Read non-secret key identifier and independent rotation count, recordId and owner; never key values.
eg.scanBrowserForCredentialValues: Compare page text and input values against fixture-owned credentials internally; return only {matches,scannedText,scannedInputs}, never the values.
eg.inventory_setup: channel_inventory uses the named setup and channel_inventory_contract below. github_inventory requires >=2 pages plus exact owned/foreign App refs and expected capability flags.
eg.channel_setup: channelName, channelId, updateBody (credential-free baseline), expected producer/consumer node accessible names, firstText, and unrelatedChannelId/unrelatedChannelDigest. Cleanup must remove only the acquired disposable channel; accept already-deleted owned resources.
eg.channel_delete: Named parent setup for EG-031. Returns a disposable owner channel plus baseline counters, request/counters/platformSend/quiesce methods, ownerSubject, and an independently retained unrelatedChannelId/unrelatedChannelDigest. Cleanup is registered before browser deletion, removes only the owned channel, and accepts an already-deleted owned resource.

eg.am_evidence: retainTurn emits schema multi-am-eg-evidence-v1, secrets_redacted:true, requests:amRequests with each actual c275-serving-v1 request receipt (serving, serving_after, started_at, ended_at, attribution, request_id), eg_receipts:[] and event/response hashes. Shared runner must ingest this schema for counts. EG-only requests never get AM ownership invented.

channel_tests_contract.prepare: eg_browser.prepare({session,actor,options:{channelTests:true},ctx}) binds the existing parent Chromium and compiled UI to the real owner cookie and EG proxy. channel_tests_contract.counters: Independent scoped nonnegative integer turns/effects/deliveries/ingress. quiesce is a bounded producer/provider/platform barrier returning those actual counts, not a sleep. channel_tests_contract.nodeTestCaptures: Read-only independent relay/provider capture of completed diagnostics scoped to this lease, initially []. Each entry has actual eg_request_id, channel_id, consumer_id, binding_id, conversation_id, agent_id, response_id, started_at, accepted_at, completed_at, first_text, admission_request_id and full amRequests. Correlate EG request -> selected binding -> provider acceptance -> actual AM admission using real trace/relay observations; never derive an AM request, request timestamp, owner or result from browser labels or expected fields. Missing trace/capture capability is BLOCKED. Capture all diagnostics so extra admissions cannot be hidden by filtering to expected requests.
channel_tests_contract.am_evidence: Original actual c275-serving-v1 request fields and owner proofs are preserved in multi-am-eg-evidence-v1. event_kind:node_test and event_identity:eg_request_id explicitly identify event_sha256 as the initiating diagnostic HTTP request hash, not a platform event ID. response_sha256 hashes the actual captured response. The exact admission_request_id must identify a real successful non-owner POST. EG process receipts remain separate. No invented platform event or requested-AM attribution.
channel_tests_contract.unknown: The browser guard forwards one real POST with retries/redirects disabled, retains its actual accepted 200 and request ID, then aborts only the downstream response. It blocks duplicate or unrelated EG mutations. The case reads a fresh real Activity stream through the other observed EG and requires the captured response/consumer/Agent/conversation tuple, completion and no delivery. Current product diagnostics lack this Activity persistence; missing tuples throw node_test_unknown_activity_reconciliation_missing. No reconcileTest result delegate, resend or invented activity frame may satisfy the clause.

channel_inventory_contract.setup: setups.channel_inventory binds the existing authentic parent fixture factory with cleanup custody before validation. Seed exactly 51..100 isolated owner records (the real list limit is 50), including selectedRecordId addressed at version>1 and missingRecordId retained without channel_id/endpoints. Seed a foreignRecordId under another synthetic owner. The selected channel has >=2 producers and >=2 consumers with distinct accessible names and known saved facts. Do not create missing-address behavior by intercepting responses. The fixture factory must use its authorized retained local storage fixture or report BLOCKED. No customer bots or production data.
channel_inventory_contract.expected: ownerSubject; channels:[{recordId,name,version,createdAt,creator,definitionDigest,addressed,channelId?}] from independently retained fixture creation/readback, with unique record IDs/names; selectedRecordId, missingRecordId, foreignRecordId; nodes:[{kind:producer|consumer,name,facts:{label:value}}]. definitionDigest hashes the exact redacted public definition from setup, creator is the stored metadata display_name or subject. Include meaningful source policy/routes and each consumer ID/provider/binding facts from the known seeded configuration. Expected data must not be populated from the case requests being checked.
channel_inventory_contract.prepare: eg_browser.prepare({session,actor,options:{channelInventory:true},ctx}) binds the parent-owned Chromium/compiled UI and real owner cookie to the actual EG proxy. Return identity.subject, egEvidence(), switchEG(replica), networkIdle() and close(). networkIdle joins finite browser requests and ignores Activity streams. No second browser/application/process; no mocked list/detail responses.
channel_inventory_contract.scanners: scanCredentialValues({value}) compares actual API bodies to fixture-owned secret values internally and returns only {scanned:true,matches}. scanBrowserForCredentialValues({page}) compares rendered text and all input values against the same runtime credentials and returns only {scannedText:true,scannedInputs:true,matches}. Scan each list page, detail, selected node and expanded legacy JSON. Never return, retain, or log secret values. These are value scanners, not case-verdict delegates.
channel_inventory_contract.effects: counters() and bounded quiesce() return independent scoped nonnegative turns/effects/deliveries/ingress. Browsing must leave every count unchanged. The browser write guard rejects any EG mutation before forwarding; cleanup removes only the exact acquired owner/foreign records and joins owned children. The parent owns final storage disposal.
channel_inventory_contract.evidence: EG-018 is eg_only: all list/pagination/detail reads retain real c275-eg-serving-v1 receipts from both EGs, including request IDs and process windows. No AM ownership or Agent turn is invented for this owner inventory. Refresh on the peer must reset to the actual first page and render exactly the returned record identities, timestamps, creator metadata and saved versions.

relay_journey_contract.setup: setups.relay_telegram/relay_discord/relay_whatsapp/relay_lark/relay_feishu/relay_slack call the existing parent EG acquire factory, with cleanup custody registered before validation. Return recordId/channelId and expected:{ownerSubject,issuer,keyId,routeId,replySender,consumerId,callbackUrl,verificationMode,conversations:[{senderId,chatId}]}. callbackUrl is the actual configured advertised NyxID callback URL; it is inspected, never used as an untrusted network target. Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp require three distinct private chat identities; Lark/Feishu/Slack require one. Telegram private chat IDs equal their senders. Seed a clean disposable source/channel, no tested event or prior model history, and zero scoped work/effects/deliveries. Use cma_codex with fresh independent conversation bindings, no existing_agent target, source_user affinity or routing fanout; partition v1 conversation or conversation_and_sender, auto_final=true, ack_after_ms=0 and source sink only. No second application, real customer bot or NyxID configuration change.
relay_journey_contract.trust: The case reads actual source records and capabilities through both EGs, checks exact issuer/key/route/callback and derives native_event, raw_event or trusted_normalized from saved flags. Telegram/Lark/Feishu use native_event; Slack uses explicit trusted_normalized; Discord/WhatsApp may use either advertised explicit mode. The selected mode must be enabled; unavailable modes stay unavailable and no automatic downgrade or flag/configuration edit is allowed. Current source/capability documents must remain identical after all turns.
relay_journey_contract.wire: platformSend receives explicit messageId/correlationId/senderId/chatId/routeId and exact text/completionText and submits once through the selected actual EG. Return accepted event identities plus actual ingress:{status,body,contentType,protocolVersion,receipt}. callbackCapture({requestId}) uses the same multi-eg-relay-wire-v1 capture/digest contract as relay_verification, plus factsBasis. For native_event/raw_event, factsBasis=raw_event and facts derive actual raw platform sender/chat/text (private messages, mentioned=false,isBotSender=false). For trusted_normalized, factsBasis=signed_normalized and mentioned/isBotSender are null: authentic normalized output does not independently prove sender kind or addressing. All other exact facts/digests join the submitted message and actual request. Never return an expected-input echo or raw tokens; original signed bytes stay in private parent custody.
relay_journey_contract.context: providerContext({eventId}) returns the actual independently captured fake-model request assembled by the real AM: {eventId,responseId,agentId,conversationId,requestCount,messages:[{role,content}]}. Text content is a string or typed text/input_text/output_text parts. Exactly one model request is permitted per simple answer. The case injects fresh EGRELAY markers in the first user message; the follow-up omits that token and must still have the original user message in its actual provider history. No marker from another conversation/case may appear. The case hashes this capture and never retains the raw transcript. A delivery contextEventIds list cannot substitute for provider input.
relay_journey_contract.delivery: The fake provider emits the case-chosen numbered completionText through the real AM/EG response path. waitForTurn supplies the full actual AM serving/owner receipts; waitForDelivery observes the real synthetic platform destination, reply sender, content digest and exactly-once count. Three contextual rows run three sequential first/follow-up pairs in distinct conversations and require six distinct events/responses, per-pair retained Agent/conversation identity, distinct pair contexts, both actual AM ingress identities and both actual EG process identities. Other rows admit one complete event. counters/drain independently require matching turns/effects/deliveries and zero pending/unknown/late work after every answer. All operations honor signal/timeoutMs; unknown transport is never resubmitted.
relay_journey_contract.external_acceptance: EG-032/033/034 retain the separate shared externalPlatformEvidence gate for designated actual-platform acceptance. Return actual multi-am-external-platform-v1 artifacts only when independently observed and authorized; synthetic local capture is not that proof. Missing capability blocks before feature action, and missing/mismatched proof prevents whole-row PASS. Authoring this case does not authorize external platform access.
relay_journey_contract.cleanup: Release only the named parent fixture and its owned public channel/provider resources; reconcile uncertain original work without replay, join provider/platform finality, and preserve cleanup failures. Parent final database disposal and the separate AM restart witness remain mandatory. Missing authentic source, signer/capture, model history, AM receipts or delivery/finality controls stay BLOCKED.

relay_verification_contract.identities: Telegram sender/bot IDs are distinct positive numeric strings; privateChat equals allowedSender and groupChat is a negative numeric ID. The denied sender probe is a correctly mentioned group message, so sender refusal is isolated from private-chat or mention inconsistencies.
relay_verification_contract.setup: setups.relay_verification binds the existing parent EG acquire factory and registers cleanup before validating its contract. Seed one empty disposable owner channel with a single verified Telegram NyxID relay source, cma_codex provider bound to real AMs, conversation_and_sender partition v1, auto_final=true, ack_after_ms=0 and source sink only. No routing fanout. expected contains issuer/keyId/ownerSubject/consumerId/replySender/botId/botUsername, distinct allowedSender/deniedSender, privateChat/groupChat and privateRoute/groupRoute/deniedRoute. Allow only the first sender, the two chats and the private/group routes, with groups=mention and default bot deny. Keep trust_normalized=false; use raw Telegram facts. Initial provider/platform counts and public Activity are empty. Never change NyxID configuration or start another application.
relay_verification_contract.platformSend: Send exactly one newly signed synthetic callback using the case's messageId, correlationId, senderId, chatId, routeId, isGroup, mentioned, isBotSender=false and exact text. Raw Telegram entities must genuinely match the mention setting. Use the existing parent's local runtime signer and source endpoint. variant=invalid_signature corrupts only the signature of an otherwise valid callback, yielding token_signature, not a malformed/expired-token substitute. A deniedRoute is still signed correctly. Return existing accepted event identities plus ingress:{status,body,contentType,protocolVersion,receipt}; negative responses return the same real ingress surface. receipt is actual c275-eg-serving-v1 with method POST and original response request_id. Never translate HTTP failures into generic outcome labels. Preserve unknown outcomes without retry/rekey.
relay_verification_contract.capture: callbackCapture({requestId}) reads the independent actual ingress capture -> {schema:multi-eg-relay-wire-v1,request_id,method,path,artifact_sha256,body_sha256,signed_headers_sha256,callback_token_sha256,reply_token_sha256,callback_body_sha256,facts}. artifact_sha256 hashes the actual sanitized capture artifact, not the supplied case input. Body/header/token digests come from transmitted bytes. signed_headers_sha256 hashes canonical JSON of the actual five x-nyxid-* callback headers (callback-token, optional user-token, message-id, platform, timestamp), sorted lowercase names; absent optional user-token is omitted. callback_body_sha256 is the decoded callback JWT claim. facts contains exactly platform,issuer,keyId,messageId,correlationId,routeId,chatId,senderId,isGroup,mentioned,isBotSender,textDigest, derived from captured claims/envelope/raw Telegram event. No expected-input echo, credentials, raw JWT or request body leaves the parent. Raw replay bytes stay only in private in-memory custody.
relay_verification_contract.replay: replayEvent({eventId,replica,signal,timeoutMs}) forwards the exact original signed headers and body once to the selected actual EG, without re-signing, changing timestamps or issuing new message/correlation IDs. Return ingress with its own actual response/request receipt. The case compares all wire digests, distinct request IDs and actual EG processes. Explicit duplicate probes occur once while original provider completion is held and once on each EG after completion; a transport exception is never retried.
relay_verification_contract.completion: holdCompletion=true holds only the fake-provider completion for the real accepted AM turn. waitForTurn({eventId,stage:accepted}) returns independently observed provider acceptance and the full actual AM serving/owner evidence required by retainTurn. releaseCompletion({eventId}) releases that hold once; waitForDelivery reads the actual synthetic platform destination/sender/content/count. completionText is chosen by the case and supplied through the fake model, not a fabricated platform answer. Each accepted event has exactly one consumer and one answer with no acknowledgement.
relay_verification_contract.finality: counters/quiesce/drain return independently observed scoped {turns,effects,deliveries,pending,unknown,lateEffects}. Before tests all are zero. While held, pending=1 and the original turn/effect remain exactly one despite duplicate intake; quiesce observes a bounded no-additional-work barrier without releasing the hold. Every negative callback leaves work/delivery counts unchanged. Final drain must yield two turns/effects/deliveries and zero pending/unknown/lateEffects. Real public Activity on both EGs retains only the two accepted source identities and exact completed Agent/consumer/response records; retained replay cannot replace them. All operations honor signal/timeoutMs. Cleanup releases any hold, reconciles unknown work, proves finality and deletes only owned public resources; parent final database disposal remains mandatory. Missing primitives stay BLOCKED.

documentation_contract.prepare: eg_browser.prepare({session,actor,options:{documentation:true},ctx}) uses the existing parent Chromium context and compiled web artifact. Return egEvidence(), switchEG(replica), networkIdle(), close(), and documentation:{publicBase,advertiseCanonical}. publicBase is the exact real EG configured advertised_api_url, normalized without a trailing slash, on a local HTTP origin; advertiseCanonical is the actual advertise_public_api_url configuration. No second browser/application/process or configuration change.
documentation_contract.public_routes: Bind actual public /event-gateway/openapi.json and /event-gateway/docs including Markdown, HTML, CSS, downloads and SVG routes to the selected real EG. Also capture reads to its admitted local publicBase origin where the backend emits absolute links. Preserve original bodies, headers, downloads and request IDs. Public page fetches omit credentials; no authentication injection is needed for these routes. The ordinary /api/event-gateway and AM session routes retain their real bindings.
documentation_contract.evidence: Capture actual c275-eg-serving-v1 before/after process/source/image windows and request IDs for public routes and both replicas. egEvidence must include navigation and Page fetch requests; APIRequestContext is not used because it bypasses page routing. switchEG genuinely changes the destination of subsequent public reads. Cases join every source/HTML/OpenAPI response to its receipt and the compiled Web source. Never relabel static Web assets or EG receipts as AM requests.
documentation_contract.behavior: The real Account -> Docs -> Event Gateway Protocol journey opens all three document sections, decodes every source-declared Mermaid diagram, follows internal anchors, and downloads the complete offered Markdown. Canonical live /docs/*.md sources are compared across EGs. Headings must match every source heading; download prose/code must match all three full sources after only known deployment-URL, anchor and Markdown-link rewriting. Link anchors and diagrams are checked separately. The native backend /docs HTML and download are also exercised on both actual EGs before returning through the product service selector.
documentation_contract.cleanup: Read-only guard rejects every nonlocal or mutating browser request. Download cleanup is registered immediately, reused after failure, and bounded to 4 MiB; response reads use the case budget. The case closes only its owned browser context/proxy and downloads. No channels, providers, bots or application processes are created. EG-only scope retains the parent restart/finality requirements.

native_telegram_contract.setup: setups.native_telegram binds parent eg.acquire and registers cleanup before validation. Seed one clean disposable native Telegram channel with recordId/channelId and expected:{ownerSubject,consumerId,botId,botUsername,allowedSender,deniedSender,privateChat,groupChat,callbackUrl,webhookSecretSha256}. The bot and two senders are distinct positive numeric strings; privateChat equals allowedSender; groupChat is a negative numeric string. Secret digests derive only parent-owned synthetic material; no Secret/API-credential read is authorized. Use cma_codex, conversation_and_sender v1, source sink, auto_final=true and ack_after_ms=0; no fanout, existing_agent target, source_user affinity or optional message/topic extensions. Exact allowlists contain one allowed sender and two chats; groups require mention and bots remain denied. Counts and Activity start empty.
native_telegram_contract.registration: platformConfiguration({platform:telegram}) returns multi-eg-telegram-registration-v1 with exactly three ordered calls: getMe, setWebhook, getWebhookInfo. Each call retains request_id, bot_id, method, status=200, artifact_sha256 and sanitized response {ok,result}. getMe result projects {id,username,is_bot}; setWebhook request projects {url,secret_sha256,allowed_updates,drop_pending_updates} and its result must be true. Preserve the actual seven allowed update kinds and drop_pending_updates=false. getWebhookInfo proves the exact saved native URL and zero pending updates. Capture real EG/fixture platform registration traffic and final readback; never synthesize activation from stored secret presence. Original authorization/token bodies stay in parent private custody and are not returned.
native_telegram_contract.wire: platformSend submits one actual native POST /v1/telegram/{channel_id} for the exact numeric-string updateId/messageId/senderId/chatId, isGroup/mentioned and text chosen by the case, plus its intended completionText. Serialize Telegram integers as numbers and actual mention entities; do not put relay envelopes on this route. Return actual ingress status/body/contentType/protocolVersion plus c275-eg-serving-v1 receipt. callbackCapture({requestId}) returns multi-eg-telegram-wire-v1 with actual method/path/request_id, artifact_sha256/body_sha256/secret_header_sha256 and parsed facts {updateId,messageId,senderId,chatId,chatType,isBotSender,mentioned,textDigest}. The secret digest must differ only for the explicit invalid_webhook_secret probe. Private and mentioned-group updates admit; each EG separately receives invalid-secret 401 callback_invalid/telegram_webhook_secret, denied-sender 202 refused/sender_denied and unmentioned-group 202 refused/group_not_addressed.
native_telegram_contract.association: nativeEventCapture({eventId}) returns multi-eg-native-event-v1 from the actual captured EG-to-AM provider request/response. Include request_id joined to the actual AM receipt; exact eventId/conversationId/responseId/agentId/consumerId; artifact_sha256, event_ref_sha256 and seal_verified; actual source, actor_id and text_sha256; verified reply {type:telegram,bot_id,chat_id,message_id,thread_id:null}. The parent verifies the real captured event_ref using its already-owned synthetic fixture key and exposes only this safe projection. Never infer the sealed reply from submitted inputs, decode an unsigned reference, read production keys or retain the raw reference in evidence. If this capture/verification primitive is absent, block. Native event IDs must equal telegram:<botId>:<updateId> and platformMessageId must equal the raw input messageId. Provider model input is independently captured via providerContext and must contain the actual admitted text with exactly one request.
native_telegram_contract.delivery: waitForDelivery retains the exact event/response, sender=botId, destination, case-chosen completion digest, count=1 and status=delivered. Include platformReceipt multi-eg-telegram-delivery-v1 with actual request_id/artifact_sha256/bot_id/method=sendMessage/status=200, sanitized request {chat_id,text_sha256}, and actual response {ok:true,result:{chat_id,message_id}}. Ordinary native replies have no quoted reply-to field; do not invent replyToMessageId from the incoming update. Original-message association is proved by the sealed reference chain, while the actual outgoing call separately proves chat, bot and answer. No actual third-party bot is required or authorized by this local row.
native_telegram_contract.finality: waitForTurn preserves full c275-serving-v1 AM requests and owner proofs; no EG process label supplies AM ownership. counters/drain return independently measured turns/effects/deliveries/pending/unknown/lateEffects. Exactly two admitted turns and deliveries, no effects for six negative probes, distinct private/group conversation and response IDs, and two actual EG processes. Both EGs read exact retained native Activity source, sender/chat and completed consumer/Agent/response with one confirmed answer. Saved configuration must remain unchanged. All parent operations honor signal/timeoutMs; uncertain transport is never resubmitted. close/cleanup reconciles exact owned work and joins provider/platform finality once, retaining any failure.

native_whatsapp_contract.setup: setups.native_whatsapp binds existing parent eg.acquire with cleanup registered before validation. Seed one clean disposable native WhatsApp channel with recordId/channelId and expected:{ownerSubject,consumerId:default,appId,accountId,phoneId,foreignAccountId,foreignPhoneId,allowedSender,deniedSender,callbackUrl,verifyTokenSha256,appSecretSha256}. IDs are distinct where contrasted and match native numeric Meta validation. Hashes derive only already-owned synthetic fixture material; never retrieve production keys or Secrets. The actual source is type whatsapp with exact app_id/waba_id/phone_number_id, sender/chat allowlists containing only allowedSender, groups=deny, no group_ids/forms/message events. Preserve native required durable default-consumer routing, conversation_and_sender v1, auto_final=true, ack_after_ms=0 and source-only delivery. No fanout, alternate destination/label or existing_agent target. Work counts and retained Activity start empty.
native_whatsapp_contract.custody: platformConfiguration({platform:whatsapp}) returns multi-eg-whatsapp-custody-v1 with two real ordered management-read captures. Each has method GET, status 200, request_id and artifact_sha256. First path /v25.0/debug_token retains only response.data is_valid/app_id/scopes; both whatsapp_business_management and whatsapp_business_messaging scopes and exact app identity are required. Second path /v25.0/<accountId>/phone_numbers has safe query {fields:id,limit:100} and response.data containing the exact phoneId. Never return debug-token query credentials or authorization headers. Captured authoring validation proves custody; webhook payloads alone do not prove app identity.
native_whatsapp_contract.challenge: webhookChallenge({replica,verification:valid|invalid,challenge}) issues one real GET /v1/whatsapp/{channel_id} with subscribe mode and case-chosen fresh challenge; only the selected synthetic verification token differs. Return ingress:{status,body,contentType,protocolVersion,receipt}. callbackCapture({requestId}) returns multi-eg-whatsapp-challenge-v1 with actual request_id/method/path/artifact_sha256, mode, query_keys, challenge_sha256 and verify_token_sha256, never raw token/query URL. Valid challenge must return 200 text/plain with exact fresh text; invalid token is 401 application/problem+json, code not_authenticated, detail native_whatsapp_verify_token. Both actual EGs receive both variants.
native_whatsapp_contract.wire: platformSend submits one native signed Meta envelope with the exact messageId/senderId/accountId/phoneId/timestamp/text/completionText provided by the case. Fresh message IDs begin wamid.; source app identity comes only from the configured signing key. Return real ingress plus independently joined event/Agent/conversation/consumer/response. callbackCapture yields multi-eg-whatsapp-wire-v1 with actual method/path/request_id, artifact_sha256/body_sha256/signature_sha256/expected_signature_sha256/signing_key_sha256 and parsed facts {accountId,phoneId,messageId,senderId,timestamp,kind:text,groupId:null,textDigest}. expected_signature_sha256 is independently computed over captured bytes using the parent-owned synthetic app key. Actual and expected signatures match except the explicit invalid_signature probe. Never copy intent labels into capture facts or expose raw keys/signatures.
native_whatsapp_contract.outcomes: One admitted private message returns HTTP200 application/json {accepted:1,refused:0}. Each EG separately receives four probes: invalid_signature -> HTTP401 not_authenticated/native_whatsapp_signature; correctly signed foreign phone -> HTTP200 {accepted:0,refused:0}; correctly signed foreign WABA -> the same ignored count; correctly signed denied sender -> HTTP200 {accepted:0,refused:1}. No probe may create another AM turn, effect or delivery. Ignored envelopes must not be mislabeled as authentication failures/refusals. The exact event ID is whatsapp:SHA256(JSON([appId,accountId,phoneId,messageId])).
native_whatsapp_contract.provider: waitForTurn preserves full actual c275-serving-v1 requests with owner proofs. nativeEventCapture uses multi-eg-native-event-v1, joined to an actual AM request_id and the exact eventId/conversationId/responseId/agentId/consumerId. It returns artifact_sha256, event_ref_sha256, seal_verified, actual source {type:whatsapp,app_id,waba_id,phone_number_id}, actor_id, actor_kind:unknown, text_sha256 and verified reply {type:whatsapp,app_id,waba_id,phone_number_id,recipient_id,message_id}. Verify the captured event_ref with already-owned synthetic fixture key custody, never submitted-input reconstruction. providerContext returns independently captured actual model input with the admitted text and exactly one request. Neither WhatsApp phone authentication nor the envelope proves the sender is human.
native_whatsapp_contract.delivery: waitForDelivery returns exact event/response, destination=allowedSender, sender=phoneId, case-chosen completion digest, count=1 and status=delivered. platformReceipt uses multi-eg-whatsapp-delivery-v1 with real request_id/artifact_sha256/method POST/path /v25.0/<phoneId>/messages/status 200. Project request {messaging_product:whatsapp,recipient_type:individual,to,context:{message_id},type:text,text:{preview_url:false,body_sha256}}. Actual response has messaging_product whatsapp, one matching contacts[].wa_id and one messages[].id starting wamid. The original-message context, original phone and actual outgoing answer all must match; retain no raw content or bearer.
native_whatsapp_contract.finality: captureEffects returns every actual effect attempt for the isolated lease, with step/eventId/responseId/platformRequestId/attempts. Exactly one answer and one attempt must join the Graph receipt. The saved ack delay is zero: unsolicited ack, read/typing, extra message or late effects fail. HTTP webhook acknowledgements are checked separately by their exact protocol results. counters/drain independently prove one turn/effect/delivery and zero pending/unknown/late work after the answer and every negative probe. Both EGs read the exact completed private native Activity with unknown actor kind, one default consumer, actual Agent/response, one confirmed answer and unchanged source. All operations honor signal/timeoutMs and uncertain transport is never replayed. Cleanup removes only owned fixtures, joins finality and preserves failures; no second application or real WhatsApp access is authorized.

native_discord_contract.setup: setups.native_discord acquires the existing parent lease and registers one shared cleanup promise before validation. Seed clean active and inactive native Discord channels with recordId/channelId and expected:{ownerSubject,consumerId:default,botId,inactiveBotId,senderId,reactorId,botSenderId,privateChat,serverChat,guildId,inactiveRecordId,inactiveChannelId,credentialSha256,sourceRevision}. All five bot/sender identities differ, private/server chats differ and inactive records differ. Each source has exact message+reaction intents 46593, scoped sender allowlist [senderId,reactorId,botSenderId], chat allowlist [privateChat,serverChat], mention-only groups and denied bot messages. Bot sender is deliberately allowlisted so a sender policy cannot masquerade as native bot rejection. Default-only durable routing, conversation_and_sender partition, auto_final:true, ack_after_ms:0, source-only replies, no history/thread extras or existing-Agent binding. Manual canary selection includes only active record; automatic activation disabled. Both records begin with empty Activity and zero work. sourceRevision preserves the native sha256:<hex> prefix from the real source authority; the separate credentialSha256 is a bare digest of parent-owned synthetic material.
native_discord_contract.blocked_transport: The current native Gateway opens the fixed wss://gateway.discord.gg/ and DiscordApi/DiscordRest use fixed Discord REST origins with no proxy. Native tests can inject internal transports, but no supported parent binary binding is established. Parent must supply an admitted local transport binding for discovery, Gateway and outgoing REST at the exact tested image. discordTransport:{schema:multi-eg-discord-local-binding-v1,source,image,artifact_sha256,rest_origin,gateway_origin}; endpoints must be loopback. Hash references the independently retained binding artifact, not a claim that a fixture bot is local. Missing binding throws native_discord_supported_local_transport_required before any dispatch. Do not modify DNS/TLS/global settings, use real Discord, start a second EG or replace Gateway with an HTTP callback. Product changes belong to the integration owner.
native_discord_contract.source_reads: Both actual EGs read capabilities, active/inactive channel and complete Activity using c275-eg-serving-v1 HTTP receipts bound to the local transport source/image. Active state must be selected and inactive not_selected with matching positive capacity and selected_records within it. Selection does not prove authentication/readiness; dynamic activation/connection fields differ across replicas and are excluded from immutable configuration equality. An EG peer can be standby/lease-contended. Native source/socket ownership and AM ownership remain separate.
native_discord_contract.gateway_snapshot: gatewaySnapshot returns multi-eg-discord-gateway-v1:{artifact_sha256,monitored_bot_ids:[botId,inactiveBotId],sessions_complete:true,observed_from,observed_until,sessions,discovery,activation}. native_lark_webhook_primitive.event: sender.sendEvent({replica,eventId,eventType,event,variant?,allowed?,timeoutMs?,signal?}) constructs schema2.0 with exact app/tenant/token header, encrypts JSON using AES-256-CBC/PKCS7 with SHA256(Encrypt Key) and fresh random16-byte IV prefixed to ciphertext, and POSTs outer {encrypt:base64(iv+ciphertext)} to /v1/native-lark/<channelId>. It signs exactly timestamp+nonce+EncryptKey+transmitted outer JSON bytes with SHA256, using x-lark-request-timestamp/x-lark-request-nonce/x-lark-signature. native_lark_webhook_primitive.challenge: sender.sendChallenge({replica,challenge,variant?,allowed?,timeoutMs?,signal?}) encrypts {type:url_verification,challenge,token} with the same actual envelope and sends no signature headers. Other actual responses, including source/provider failures, retain their status and cannot become acceptance.

Caller cancellation and sender.close abort and join current HTTP operations; closed senders refuse new work. close reuses one promise and clears held key material after joined work. No raw keys, signatures, plaintext event content or ciphertext are retained in evidence.

These receivers are protocol test doubles and do not execute the Rust native handler or establish integrated runtime acceptance.
